subject.title: fix(mcp): standalone apps stop hanging on stalled gateway requests

question: Should a session-MCP runtime keep a current shared catalog refresh alive after its final operation waiter detaches, so it can warm the cache and preserve reusable sessions until invalidation or runtime disposal?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent, but this choice determines resource lifetime, cancellation semantics, cache warming, and behavior for stalled transports across all callers; tests cannot determine the intended runtime ownership contract.

options.title: Confirm runtime-owned refreshes
options.body: Keep the branch’s model: caller cancellation detaches only that caller, while the runtime aborts work only when the generation becomes obsolete or the runtime is disposed.

options.title: Abort refreshes without waiters
options.body: Restore cancellation when the final operation waiter detaches, accepting lost cache warming in exchange for tighter resource release.

recommendation.title: Confirm runtime-owned refreshes
recommendation.body: Keep the branch’s model: caller cancellation detaches only that caller, while the runtime aborts work only when the generation becomes obsolete or the runtime is disposed.

likelyOwner.reason: They reviewed the adjacent timeout contract and explicitly identified that the remaining decision belongs with the MCP runtime owner; no more authoritative owner was established from the supplied history.
